:::{#rem-overfitting-tradeoff}
#### Overfitting and the trade-off

By @rem-generalization-error,
the expected squared prediction error at $x$
is the squared bias plus the variance plus the noise variance.
Under a [bias--variance trade-off](#def-bias-variance-tradeoff),
moving to the next, more flexible procedure
lowers that error when the squared bias falls by more than the variance rises,
and raises it otherwise.
The error is often smallest at an intermediate flexibility
[@james2021islr2e, sec. 2.2.2],
but not always:
if the true mean function is a candidate of the least flexible procedure,
that procedure's squared bias can be zero,
and then no more flexible procedure has a smaller squared bias,
and under the trade-off none has a smaller variance,
so none has a smaller expected squared prediction error.
[Overfitting](#def-overfitting) is the flexible side of the smallest error:
a procedure there has lowered its squared bias
by less than it has raised its variance.

:::
